notice: Public-evidence status is not an effectiveness or legal-compliance rating.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province should apologize, prompt comparable health-system apologies and lead a comprehensive system-wide anti-racism response with common language and clear institutional responsibilities.

The Province, working with Indigenous peoples, should establish policy foundations and legislative changes that require anti-racism and embed cultural safety consistently with the Declaration Act and UN Declaration.
responsible_organizations: Indigenous peoples in British Columbia (consultation and cooperation partners)
recommendations.owner_review_reason: Completion depends on the breadth and operational effect of multiple laws, policies and practices, not enactment alone.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province, First Nations governing and representative bodies and Métis Nation British Columbia should jointly establish a legislatively recognized B.C. Indigenous Health Officer with a structured relationship to the Provincial Health Officer.
responsible_organizations: First Nations governing bodies and representative organizations
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The public evidence stops at discussions and cannot resolve present institutional status.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province, First Nations governing and representative bodies and Métis Nation British Columbia should jointly establish a legislatively recognized, adequately funded Indigenous Health Representative and Advocate office for navigation, early intervention and dispute resolution.
responsible_organizations: First Nations governing bodies and representative organizations
recommendations.owner_review_reason: Current establishment, authority and funding of the proposed office remain unresolved.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province, First Nations governing and representative bodies and Métis Nation British Columbia should jointly improve patient complaint processes for individual and systemic Indigenous-specific racism.
responsible_organizations: First Nations governing bodies and representative organizations

recommendations.short_summary: Parties to bilateral and tripartite First Nations health agreements should address unmet commitments through renewed structures and agreements consistent with the Declaration Act.
recommendations.owner_review_reason: Agreement-level scope and governance authority require careful review rather than a single completion label.

recommendations.short_summary: The Ministry should establish a senior Métis health relationship table and direct health authorities to enter measurable Letters of Understanding with Métis Nation British Columbia and Métis Chartered Communities.

Health-system policymakers, authorities, regulators, facilities, review boards and education programs should adopt an Indigenous cultural-safety and humility accreditation standard developed with Indigenous peoples.
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The recommendation's universal adoption scope is broader than the evidence of standard creation and assessment development.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province should establish a system-wide Indigenous cultural-safety, health-rights and anti-racism measurement framework with appropriate Indigenous data governance.
responsible_organizations: First Nations governing bodies and representative organizations
recommendations.owner_review_reason: No completed public framework or dashboard was located.

recommendations.short_summary: Hospital design should be undertaken with local Indigenous peoples and host Nations and include culturally appropriate ceremonial spaces, art, signage and territorial acknowledgement.
responsible_organizations: local Indigenous peoples and host Nations
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The recommendation is system-wide, while accessible evidence is project-specific.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province should extend Public Interest Disclosure Act protections across health-sector employees to strengthen safe disclosure of wrongdoing, including Indigenous-specific racism.
The B.C. Ombudsperson should prioritize Indigenous-specific racism in health care, seek partner input, improve fairness-related activities and report publicly on progress.
responsible_organizations: Office of the Ombudsperson of British Columbia

recommendations.short_summary: The Province should create an Associate Deputy Minister for Indigenous Health with authority to support Ministry leadership in implementing the recommendations.
Government, health authorities, post-secondary institutions, regulators and health-service organizations should recruit Indigenous people into senior roles capable of leading system change.
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The recommendation spans a much broader institutional set than the health-authority evidence alone.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province, Indigenous governing and representative bodies, Métis Nation British Columbia, the PHO and Indigenous Health Officer should create a robust Indigenous pandemic-response structure that resolves jurisdictional issues and upholds the UN Declaration.
responsible_organizations: First Nations governing bodies and representative organizations
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The named Indigenous Health Officer role is itself unresolved and the joint governance structure is not public.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province should take immediate measures responding to the MMIWG Calls for Justice and the specific health-care experiences and needs of Indigenous women identified by the review.
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The recommendation is broad and cross-government; selected measures cannot stand for the entire obligation.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province and FNHA should demonstrate progress in expanding access to culturally safe mental-health, wellness and substance-use services.
recommendations.owner_review_reason: Access progress and program-level funding require careful scope control.

recommendations.short_summary: All B.C. post-secondary health-profession programs should have mandatory strategies and targets for Indigenous recruitment, enrolment, graduation and safer learning environments.
responsible_organizations: B.C. universities and colleges with health-profession programs
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The evidence is institution-specific and outcome language may not be consistently measured.

recommendations.short_summary: A centre should provide open access to anti-racism, cultural-safety and trauma-informed standards, evidence, tools, policy expertise and collaborative capacity.
responsible_organizations: Government of British Columbia and health-system partners
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The identity and mandate of any completed centre remain ambiguous.

recommendations.short_summary: The health system should implement a refreshed, co-developed, standardized and mandatory anti-racism, cultural-humility and trauma-informed training approach that absorbs existing San'yas training.
responsible_organizations: First Nations governing and representative bodies
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The recommendation's standardization, co-development and system-wide reach exceed the available activity evidence.

recommendations.short_summary: All B.C. post-secondary health-practitioner programs should include mandatory teaching on Indigenous-specific racism, colonialism, trauma-informed care, Indigenous health and the UN Declaration standard.
responsible_organizations: B.C. universities and colleges with health-practitioner programs
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The evidence demonstrates examples, not universal implementation.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province, with Indigenous peoples, should pursue truth-telling and public education, including age-appropriate resources on Indigenous health and wellness before and after European arrival.
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The evidence is strong for specified elements but not for the whole recommendation.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province and Indigenous partners should establish joint degrees in medicine and Indigenous medicine, and a comparable joint nursing degree.
responsible_organizations: First Nations governing bodies and representative organizations
recommendations.owner_review_reason: The relationship between the current programs and the report's specific joint-degree design requires owner judgment.

recommendations.short_summary: The Province should establish a task team for at least 24 months to propel implementation, work with senior Ministry leadership, uphold consultation and cooperation standards and report publicly.
recommendations.owner_review_reason: Task-team completion is clear, but the ongoing public-accountability component has a documented coverage limitation.

themes.title: Governance and Indigenous leadership
themes.strongest_implementation_evidence: Formal senior roles, tables, agreements and task structures are publicly documented.
themes.major_reporting_gap: No single source measures how consistently these structures changed decision-making across the system.

themes.title: Complaints, advocacy and oversight
themes.strongest_implementation_evidence: PIDA coverage was extended to health-authority employees and complaint/oversight mechanisms are documented.
themes.major_reporting_gap: Complaint access and statutory coverage are not outcome measures for patient experience or speak-up culture.

themes.title: Law, standards and accountability
themes.strongest_implementation_evidence: New professional legislation and a First Nations-led cultural-safety standard are concrete outputs.
themes.major_reporting_gap: Universal adoption, operational compliance and accreditation use remain distributed or incomplete.

themes.title: Data, measurement and public reporting
themes.strongest_implementation_evidence: Measurement and reporting work has been publicly described.
themes.major_reporting_gap: A comprehensive current public recommendation-by-recommendation ledger and completed system dashboard were not located.

themes.title: Facilities, access and services
themes.strongest_implementation_evidence: Specific facilities and service changes show operational examples.
themes.major_reporting_gap: Project examples do not establish consistent provincewide implementation.

themes.title: Gender-specific response
themes.major_reporting_gap: Recommendation-specific outcomes are not reported comprehensively.

themes.title: Workforce and leadership
themes.strongest_implementation_evidence: Indigenous leadership appointments and workforce initiatives are documented.
themes.major_reporting_gap: Cross-sector retention, representation and outcome measures are incomplete.

themes.title: Education, training and institutional capacity
themes.strongest_implementation_evidence: Training tools, program changes and institutional initiatives are documented.
themes.major_reporting_gap: Participation does not establish effectiveness, universal reach or sustained behavioural change.
